Explanation: The core value unit is a specific accommodation stay that a traveler can compare and reserve for particular dates and conditions.
Booking.com B.V. operates the accommodation marketplace, including search, ranking, booking, reviews, customer support and an expanding payment layer.
Booking.com must turn millions of independent accommodation offers into a searchable and bookable set of options for each trip.
Booking.com primarily earns from commissions on reservations and can also monetize visibility through paid placement and related advertising products.
Booking.com has to keep travelers and properties transacting through the platform while limiting fraud, poor experiences, cancellations and off-platform leakage.
Booking.com matches traveler intent with bookable accommodation and determines how offers are ordered and surfaced before a reservation is made.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Search / Book — Travelers send destination, dates and preferences into Booking.com and make the reservation through the platform. | → Consumer · Ranked Stays — Booking.com returns an ordered set of bookable properties using filters and recommendation systems, with paid placements identified separately. | ← Provider · Rooms / Fee — Accommodation providers supply rooms, rates, availability and content, and pay Booking.com commission on qualifying reservations. | → Provider · Bookings / Pay — Booking.com sends confirmed reservations and demand to properties; where Payments by Booking.com is used, it can also collect guest funds and pay the property, while agency bookings can still be paid directly at the property. | ← Partner · Inventory Sync — Connectivity partners keep rates, availability, content and reservations synchronized between property systems and Booking.com.

Explanation: Booking.com sets marketplace rules and uses reviews, performance data, commercial programs and other signals to govern which properties are shown and in what order.
Booking.com attracts repeat demand through direct search, brand marketing and the Genius loyalty program, while also buying traffic from external channels.
Core activities include search and ranking, booking conversion, fraud and trust controls, customer service, partner support and payment facilitation.
Booking.com’s key resources are global traveler demand, booking and review data, brand recognition, software and its provider network.
Travelers are people searching for and booking accommodation for leisure, family, work or other trips.
Travelers want to find an available place that fits their dates, location, budget and preferences.
Travelers gain broad supply, price comparison, filters, verified reviews, flexible policies and a standardized booking flow.
Large choice can create comparison overload, while changing prices, policies and property quality make the decision harder.
Travelers search, compare and reserve a stay through Booking.com; payment may be handled by Booking.com or by the accommodation depending on the booking setup.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Search / Book — Travelers send destination, dates and preferences into Booking.com and make the reservation through the platform. | ← Owner · Ranked Stays — Booking.com returns an ordered set of bookable properties using filters and recommendation systems, with paid placements identified separately. | ← Provider · Stay — The accommodation provider, not Booking.com, delivers the actual room or home and the local hospitality service to the traveler.

Explanation: Travelers narrow the marketplace by destination, dates, party size, budget, property type, review score and other preferences.
Travelers use Booking.com’s mobile apps and websites to search, book, manage reservations and contact support.
Travelers search, compare offers, book, complete the stay and can then leave a verified review.
Travelers contribute trip dates, destination, preferences, payment capability and attention to the marketplace.
Providers are hotels, motels, resorts, hostels, apartment operators, home hosts and professional property managers that supply the accommodation.
Providers want to turn perishable room or home availability into paid stays while controlling rates, policies and inventory.
Booking.com gives providers access to global demand and tools that can improve occupancy and conversion, especially for independent properties.
Providers give up commission and may face intense competition for ranking, price and visibility inside the marketplace.
Providers supply rooms, rates and availability to Booking.com and owe commission on eligible completed or charged reservations under their agreement.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Rooms / Fee — Accommodation providers supply rooms, rates, availability and content, and pay Booking.com commission on qualifying reservations. | ← Owner · Bookings / Pay — Booking.com sends confirmed reservations and demand to properties; where Payments by Booking.com is used, it can also collect guest funds and pay the property, while agency bookings can still be paid directly at the property. | → Consumer · Stay — The accommodation provider, not Booking.com, delivers the actual room or home and the local hospitality service to the traveler.

Explanation: Properties must meet contractual, content, licensing and operational requirements to become and remain bookable.
Properties manage Booking.com directly through the Extranet or indirectly through approved connectivity software and APIs.
Providers set rates and availability, maintain property content and policies, receive reservations and deliver the stay.
Providers contribute the physical accommodation, live inventory, prices, policies, photos and local service capability.
Connectivity Partners are professional channel-manager, PMS and software providers that connect accommodation systems to Booking.com.
Their job is to keep property content, rates, availability and reservations synchronized between Booking.com and the systems properties already use.
Connectivity partners become more useful to accommodation clients when one interface can manage Booking.com alongside other sales channels.
They must keep integrations current, map rooms and rates correctly, protect payment and personal data and adapt to Booking.com API changes.
Connectivity software exchanges live inventory and reservation data with Booking.com on behalf of connected accommodation providers.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Inventory Sync — Connectivity partners keep rates, availability, content and reservations synchronized between property systems and Booking.com.

Explanation: Booking.com requires connectivity providers to meet onboarding, certification, security and ongoing technical requirements.
Connectivity partners use Booking.com’s Connectivity APIs and Provider Portal rather than the traveler-facing marketplace interface.
They synchronize inventory, rates and reservations, map property data and expose Booking.com functions inside their own software.
They contribute property-management systems, channel-management software, APIs and operational property data.
